newsitem.title: NORWAY: FOCUS - Investcorp buys Helly Hansen sportswear.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Investcorp buys Helly Hansen sportswear.

text.p: Bahrain-based international investment group Investcorp Bank EC will buy Norwegian outdoor and sportswear company Helly Hansen under an agreement announced on Friday.
Helly Hansen, a brand name with expanding sales especially in the United States, is now owned 50-50 by Norwegian industrial holding company Aker RGI ASA and Orkla ASA, a branded goods conglomerate.

Aker RGI said that it was selling its stake for 430 million crowns ($61.7 million). Following a private placement in a newly-established company, Helly Hansen Holding, Orkla's stake in Helly Hansen will be watered down to 30 percent and Investcorp will own 70 percent.

Investcorp was formed in 1982 to service the needs of cash-rich investors in the Gulf. It has made a reputation for turning round troubled companies, including Italian luxury goods group Gucci. Analysts, who value Helly Hansen at about one billion crowns, said the deal was good business for Aker RGI. The group bought its 50 percent holding little more than two years ago for 125 million crowns.
"Aker RGI had said they would sell for betwen 400 and 500 million crowns," one analyst said. "They got the price they expected."
Aker RGI announced in February it had started negotiations for a sale of its holding in Helly Hansen to concentrate on core operations.

Helly Hansen has made considerable improvements in the past two years. Total 1996 sales came to 941 million crowns and the company made an operating profit of 101 million crowns, up from 22 million crowns in 1995.
"Helly Hansen has had a dramatic result improvement," one analyst said. "It is a very well-known brand name. It clearly has value of its own. It is a good investment object."
"They should make a pre-tax profit of 90 to 130 million crowns this year," another analyst said.

"Now Helly Hansen will still have two stable owners and it will give them a chance to develop their position. Helly Hansen also needs more capital and they will apparently get it through the private placement," he said.

Company officials said it had been important in the change of ownership to bring in an owner which could make a professional contribution towards developing Helly Hansen's outdoor brand on international markets.
"Investcorp has achieved substantial success in developing brand-name firms in such sectors as sports and leisure on a global basis," Aker RGI said.
Helly Hansen, with about 500 employees, will continue to have its headquarters in Norway. The agreement between the three parties will enter into force in May, subject to official approval.
